body:
This PR addresses the project structure refactoring requirements by creating a clean separation between frontend and backend code, with the frontend ready for GitHub Pages deployment and backend providing mock APIs.

## Changes Made

### 🎨 Frontend (Client) Structure
- **Moved all React code to `client/` folder**: Relocated `src/`, `public/`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` and dependencies
- **GitHub Pages ready**: Maintained existing homepage configuration (`https://kumarbhakta81.github.io/ordermanagement`) 
- **Build verification**: Confirmed production builds work correctly from the new location
- **Preserved functionality**: All existing React components, routing, and Material-UI integration remain intact

### 🚀 Backend API Server
- **Created comprehensive Express.js backend** in `backend/` folder with proper MVC structure
- **Implemented all documented endpoints** from `backend_documentation.md`:
  - Orders management (`/api/orders`)
  - Products catalog (`/api/products`) 
  - Customer management (`/api/customers`)
  - Inventory tracking (`/api/inventory`)
  - Authentication (`/api/auth`)
  - Dashboard analytics (`/api/dashboard`)
- **Mock data implementation**: Realistic dummy data that simulates real database operations
- **Easy API replacement**: Structured for seamless integration with real databases and services
- **CORS enabled**: Ready for frontend integration during development

### 📚 Documentation Updates
- **Comprehensive README.md**: Updated with new project structure, setup instructions, and development workflows
- **Backend README.md**: Detailed API documentation with endpoint specifications and usage examples
- **Clear separation guidance**: Instructions for frontend and backend development workflows

### 🛠 Development Experience
- **Independent development**: Frontend and backend can be developed separately
- **Hot reloading**: Both `npm start` (client) and `npm run dev` (backend) support live reloading
- **Clean builds**: Updated `.gitignore` to properly exclude build artifacts and dependencies

## Project Structure
```
ordermanagement/
├── client/                 # React frontend (GitHub Pages ready)
│   ├── src/               # Components, pages, services
│   ├── public/            # Static assets  
│   └── package.json       # Frontend dependencies
├── backend/               # Express.js API server
│   ├── src/routes/        # API endpoints
│   ├── src/utils/         # Mock data
│   └── package.json       # Backend dependencies
└── README.md              # Updated documentation
```

## Verification
- ✅ Client builds successfully and maintains GitHub Pages compatibility
- ✅ Backend API serves mock data correctly on all endpoints
- ✅ Both components tested independently
- ✅ Documentation is comprehensive and up-to-date

## Future Integration
The mock backend is designed for easy replacement with real implementations:
- Replace `src/utils/mockData.js` with database models
- Add authentication middleware
- Implement business logic in service layers
- Connect to external APIs

This structure provides a solid foundation for scaling the application while maintaining clean separation of concerns.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Refactor the project structure to separate frontend and backend code:
> 
> 1. Create a new folder named `client` for all frontend-related work. Move all existing frontend code (previously in `functions` or similar folders) into `client`.
> 2. Ensure the frontend is deployable via GitHub Pages. Adjust configuration as needed so the client folder can be used as the source for GitHub Pages deployment.
> 3. Create a new folder named `backend` containing all backend business logic. Instead of connecting to real APIs, implement dummy API endpoints or data to mimic the actual backend processes. The backend should be structured for easy replacement with real APIs in the future.
> 
> Document any changes in README.md.
> 
> Goal: Clean separation of client and backend code, with the client ready for GitHub Pages deployment and backend using mock data/APIs.

This PR implements a comprehensive Brand Kit UI that allows users to configure their brand colors, typography, watermark settings, and logo with real-time live preview functionality, now fully integrated with the existing authentication system.

## Key Features Implemented

**Color Management**
- Primary, Secondary, and Accent color pickers using Popover + react-colorful integration
- HexColorPicker component with live color preview and hex code display
- Real-time color updates reflected in the live preview card

**Typography Controls**
- Font family input field with instant preview updates
- Live preview shows selected font applied to sample quote text

**Watermark System**
- Toggle switch to enable/disable watermark functionality
- Conditional watermark text input (only shown when enabled)
- Watermark appears in live preview with opacity styling when active

**Logo Upload**
- File input with drag-and-drop styling and validation
- Supports PNG, JPG, and SVG files up to 2MB
- Avatar component shows logo preview with fallback upload icon
- API endpoint `/api/uploads/logo` handles file processing and returns data URLs

**Live Preview Card**
- Real-time preview showing sample Winston Churchill quote
- Dynamic styling based on selected brand colors and font
- Background color tinting using primary color
- Border styling with accent color
- Watermark positioning and opacity
- Logo display when uploaded

**Persistence & API**
- `/api/brand-kit` endpoint for saving and loading brand kit configurations
- Form state management with React hooks
- Success/error handling with user feedback
- Brand kit data persists between page loads

**Authentication Integration**
- Brand Kit now accessible through the main dashboard after user login
- Maintains compatibility with existing auth flow and user management
- Accessible via both `/settings/brand-kit` and `/brand-kit` routes for flexibility
- Integrated with the dashboard's navigation system

**Navigation & UX**
- Integrated with existing dashboard navigation and auth system
- Responsive grid layout for desktop viewing
- Loading states and form validation
- Clean, professional UI using Tailwind CSS and Radix UI components
- Seamless user experience from login through brand configuration

## Technical Implementation

The implementation includes:
- Next.js 15 with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4
- Custom UI component library (Button, Input, Popover, Switch, Avatar, etc.)
- React state management for form handling and live preview updates
- File upload handling with client-side preview generation
- CSS custom properties for theme integration
- Proper TypeScript interfaces and error handling
- Full integration with existing authentication and dashboard systems
- Resolved merge conflicts while preserving functionality from both branches

## Merge Conflict Resolution

Successfully resolved conflicts between the Brand Kit implementation and the main branch's authentication system:
- Merged dependency configurations to include both auth and Brand Kit packages
- Integrated UI components with existing shadcn/ui design system
- Preserved authentication flow while adding Brand Kit functionality
- Maintained backward compatibility with existing routes and navigation

## Screenshots

### Brand Kit Interface
![Brand Kit Initial View](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3d6e4b7-2a11-4818-ba39-4459235252fd)

### Live Preview with Custom Settings
![Brand Kit with Changes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c306dd0-5d33-4817-ae3c-fecaefd8cda3)

The screenshots demonstrate the working color pickers, font controls, watermark toggle functionality, and the live preview updating in real-time as settings change.

Fixes #15.

# Complete trading bot setup with Linux-compatible launch scripts and authentication fixes

## Summary

This PR adds Linux-compatible bash equivalents to the existing PowerShell launch scripts and documents the required environment configuration changes for proper JWT authentication.

**Key Changes:**
- **`launch-bot.sh`**: Bash equivalent of `launch-bot.ps1` with proper environment variable loading from `.env.local`
- **`start-clean.sh`**: Bash equivalent of `start-clean.ps1` with filtered console output and compact logging
- **Fixed bash syntax**: Resolved environment variable name issues (periods → double underscores) for proper bash compatibility
- **Environment variable handling**: Proper loading and parsing of configuration from `.env.local`

**Required Manual Changes** (not in PR due to `.env.local` being gitignored):
- Change `AUTH_ALLOW=0` to `AUTH_ALLOW=1` in `.env.local` to enable runtime JWT acquisition
- Add `BOT_ALERT_WEBHOOK=https://discord.com/api/webhooks/YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL_HERE` placeholder

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Test bash scripts end-to-end**: Run `./launch-bot.sh` and verify the bot starts properly in SHADOW mode
- [ ] **Verify JWT authentication**: Confirm that with `AUTH_ALLOW=1` the health endpoint (`/healthz`) shows `"ok": true` instead of "JWT missing"  
- [ ] **Test start-clean.sh filtering**: Run `./start-clean.sh --checklist-only` and verify log filtering works correctly
- [ ] **Apply manual .env.local changes**: Set `AUTH_ALLOW=1` and add `BOT_ALERT_WEBHOOK` as documented above
- [ ] **Verify connectivity probe**: Ensure the connectivity probe passes when `SKIP_CONNECTIVITY_PROBE=false`

### Notes

⚠️ **Authentication Issue Not Fully Resolved**: While the connectivity probe successfully obtains JWT tokens with the updated configuration, the main bot's health endpoint still showed "JWT missing" during testing. This may require additional investigation into how the main `Program.cs` handles JWT authentication vs. the connectivity probe.

**Link to Devin run**: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/28233c734d57491193647c111fa713f7  
**Requested by**: @kevinsuero072897-collab

The bash scripts have been tested for basic functionality but may need additional validation for edge cases and full equivalency with the PowerShell versions.

author: jjaffeux
body:
Uses the timestamp at the moment where the user hits send for the created_at value of the chat message. This should ensure very consistent ordering.

The implementation is simple:
- collects the timestamp and send it in the request (client_created_at)
- if client_created_at is present and valid, set it as created_at when creating the message

I suspect that we could end up in a situation where a message is routed to a slower worker and even if sent before an other message could end up being persisted later which would cause ordering issues.
